sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Base look and glass panel helpers
sections.what: Sets up Tailwind, makes the background dark and text light across the site, uses monospace for all headings, and defines glass-panel styles with blur and thin borders in several colors.
sections.why: Gives the site its dark, layered look in one place.
sections.watch_out: The color variables at the top are defined here but are not used within this file, so changing them may do nothing.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Glow, shine, and transition helpers
sections.what: Adds helper classes for soft colored glows, a thin inner highlight, and a smooth 0.14 second transition used for hover effects.
sections.why: Gives buttons and cards a consistent feel when hovered.
sections.watch_out: Glow shadows are also defined in the Tailwind config, so changing one may not change the other.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar
sections.title: Scrollbar width
sections.what: Makes scrollbars 6 pixels thick in browsers that support these rules.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches the thin, dark look.
sections.watch_out: Firefox ignores these rules and uses its own scrollbar.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-track
sections.title: Scrollbar track color
sections.what: Colors the groove the scrollbar slides in with a near-black fill.
sections.why: Likely reason: blends into the dark background.
sections.watch_out: Uses a fixed color value instead of the palette name, so it will not follow palette changes.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb
sections.title: Scrollbar handle color
sections.what: Colors the draggable part of the scrollbar lime green with rounded ends.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover
sections.title: Scrollbar handle on hover
sections.what: Makes the handle a slightly lighter lime when the mouse is over it.
sections.why: Gives visual feedback that it can be dragged.

sections.name: ::selection
sections.title: Text highlight color and moving gradient keyframes
sections.what: Makes selected text lime with dark letters. Defines a 15 second loop that slides a background gradient back and forth.
sections.why: Likely reason: adds a subtle sense of motion to backgrounds.
sections.watch_out: Continuous animation uses processing power, and no way to turn it off is visible here.

sections.name: .animated-gradient
sections.title: Moving blue-to-lime background panel
sections.what: Applies the gradient animation to any element with this class, used behind hero and section backgrounds on several pages.
sections.why: Adds visual interest to large areas.
sections.watch_out: Each use runs its own animation loop, so many uses on one page add work for the browser.

summary: The global style sheet that sets the dark background, monospace headings, glass-panel looks, scrollbars, text selection, and a moving gradient for the whole site.
purpose: Defines the shared look that every page inherits, plus a few helper classes that pages can add to elements.
why: Putting shared styles in one place keeps every page consistent.
how: Tailwind's base rules load first. Then the body and headings get the dark background, light text, and monospace font. Helper classes for glass panels, glows, and transitions are added. Finally, scrollbar, selection, and gradient animation rules apply across the site.
inputs: Class names used in the page files, and the Tailwind build.
outputs: The site's global styles in the browser.
risks: Scrollbar and gradient rules only work in some browsers. Animation runs continuously and uses processing power. Some values are fixed colors rather than palette names.
debug: If the background or headings look wrong, check the body and headings rules first. If a glass panel looks flat, check that the class name is spelled exactly. Test scrollbars in Chrome and in Firefox, since Firefox ignores the webkit rules.
